arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Spinelli asserted that parties agree retirement funds are set aside for when an individual stops working.
Ms. Spinelli stated that funds in an inherited IRA do not meet that specific definition.
Mr. Shanmugam argued that the Bankruptcy Code's plain terms exempt funds in tax-exempt retirement accounts.
Justice Kagan noted that inherited funds cannot be added to and must be depleted over time.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the Bankruptcy Code's retirement funds exemption. The core issue is whether inherited IRA assets fit the statutory definition of funds set aside for retirement.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case want the Court to rule that inherited IRAs are not retirement funds and thus lack bankruptcy protection.
the opposing sides want the Court to rule that inherited IRAs are retirement funds and retain bankruptcy protection.

sections.heading: What each side says
